en.title: Blade Runner 2099 and The Hunting Wives: Your Next Binge Is Here
en.summary: Don't let international borders keep you from your next obsession. We're breaking down the must-watch US dramas landing on UK screens this week, from gritty sci-fi to Southern gothic secrets.
en.body:
Navigating the global streaming landscape can feel like a mission in itself, especially when that must-see US drama seems perpetually out of reach. Thankfully, savvy deals between US platforms and UK broadcasters mean we're no longer left in the dark ages of delayed releases. This week, two highly anticipated series are making their mark, offering binge-worthy content for every kind of fan.

Get ready to saddle up for a return trip to Maple Brook, Texas, with **The Hunting Wives** Season 2 premiering on November 26th. Based on May Cobb's bestselling novel, the Netflix drama plunges us back into a world of wealth, secrets, and dangerous games. Last season, Sophie found herself drawn into the orbit of the enigmatic Margo and her clique of seemingly perfect housewives, only to discover the deadly truths lurking beneath the surface. Now, in Season 2, Sophie and Margo are on the outs, but the narrative demands their reunion. As old secrets resurface and new adversaries emerge, the central question remains: who is truly in control, the hunters or the hunted? The series promises to delve deeper into the psychological manipulations and escalating stakes that defined its compelling first outing.

Meanwhile, the iconic **Blade Runner** universe expands with **Blade Runner 2099** on Prime Video. Set fifty years after the events of *Blade Runner 2049*, this sci-fi spectacle envisions a reborn Los Angeles, but one shaped by forces beyond human control. The official synopsis hints at a fugitive named Cora, portrayed by **Hunter Schafer**, who takes on the identity of a Blade Runner in a desperate bid to stop running. Her path inevitably crosses with Olwen, a Replicant played by the legendary **Michelle Yeoh**, who is mere days from expiration. This unlikely pairing suggests a narrative rich with existential themes, stunning visuals, and the philosophical quandaries that have defined the franchise since its inception. The chemistry between Schafer and Yeoh is poised to be a major draw.

## A Year of Espionage and Intrigue

Beyond these immediate releases, 2026 is shaping up to be a banner year for espionage and spy thrillers. While details are still emerging, the landscape is heating up with anticipated returns and exciting new entrants. **The Agency**, starring **Michael Fassbender**, has already captivated audiences with its second season dropping on Paramount+ this past June, continuing its exploration of deep-cover operatives and high-stakes deception. We're also seeing buzz around series like **Citadel**, returning for its second season, and other intriguing prospects such as **Agent Kim Reactivated** and **Ponies**, which follows two secretaries at the US embassy in 1977 Moscow who lead double lives as spies. Even Netflix is bolstering its spy thriller roster, with shows like **The Night Agent** and the recently added **Black Doves** setting a high bar for political intrigue and international flair. The genre thrives on complex protagonists and plots that keep viewers guessing, and the upcoming slate promises to deliver exactly that.

## What to Watch For Next

With **The Hunting Wives** Season 2 and **Blade Runner 2099** now on our radar, the focus shifts to how these narratives will unfold. Will Sophie and Margo find common ground, or will their conflict escalate beyond repair? And what new threats await Cora and Olwen in the dystopian future of *Blade Runner 2099*? Keep an eye on official announcements for any further casting news or plot details regarding other 2026 spy series as they emerge.

content_raw: We've all faced the disappointment of finding a US drama we really want to watch, only for it not to be available in the UK. The US is constantly creating must-see entertainment content and you might be thinking that these programs are only available to US audiences — but that's not the case. Thanks to these US streaming platforms securing deals with UK broadcasters like Sky and ITV, we can now watch award-winning content from a variety of genres. Although the UK isn't guaranteed the same release date as those across the pond, it saves you from waiting an age until they reach UK screens. Here are the US dramas available to watch on both UK channels and streaming this week, as well as our top picks. The Hunting Wives season 2 (Image credit: Dana Hawley/Netflix © 2026) Saddle up and put your cowboy boots on as we're heading back to Maple Brook, Texas on 26 November for the second season of The Hunting Wives. Based on the bestselling novel by May Cobb, the Netflix drama follows Sophie (Brittany Snow) who grows close to wealthy socialite Margo (Malin Akerman) and her clique of housewives that hide deadly secrets. Now in season 2, Sophie and Margo are on the outs, but old secrets and new enemies force them to reunite. However, as they play their dangerous games, the question arises: are they the hunters or the hunted? Blade Runner 2099 (Image credit: Clay Enos/Prime) Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer star in this sci-fi series from the iconic Blade Runner franchise. The official plot synopsis reads: "Fifty years after the events of Blade Runner 2049 , Los Angeles has been reborn, just not by humanity. Cora (Schafer), a fugitive in a final bid to stop running, takes on one last identity: a Blade Runner. Forced to partner with Olwen (Yeoh), a Replicant days from dying, she hunts down a runaway hiding a truth that could collapse their fragile city." All episodes of Blade Runner 2099 premiere on Prime Video on 25 November. Tracker season 4 Tracker season 4 sees Justin Hartley return as Colter Shaw, a skilled survivalist and tracker, who uses his instincts to help law enforcement and citizens find missing people. In the opening episode, which drops on Disney+ on 25 November, Colter unearths a dangerous criminal operation at the Port of Los Angeles during his search for a boy's missing father.
